Treatment summary
Patient presented following a sideswipe collision that occurred during a lane change, with complaints of neck pain,
stiffness, and headache consistent with a whiplash-type mechanism. The reported symptoms are in keeping with the
kind and force of the impact described. Over the course of twenty visits, care consisted of manual therapy, guided
range-of-motion exercises, and a home stretching program, following a typical and expected progression. Pain and
mobility improved steadily, and visit frequency was reduced accordingly as symptoms resolved. Physical examination
revealed reduced cervical range of motion and paraspinal muscle tenderness, which support the reported injury.
Other neurological screening and imaging-related assessments were within normal limits. The patient mentioned a
remote, minor strain to the same region years ago, which had fully resolved without lasting limitation. Billing records
reflect single, appropriately spaced charges for each service with no duplicated entries. At discharge, the patient was
improved, with residual stiffness only at end range and a plan for self-directed exercise.
</page>
